glm.feedback:
## Findings

**1. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium**
File: `plugins/shipwright-build/scripts/hooks/cleanup-review-scratch-on-code-reviewer-failure.py` (`resolve_shared_root`, ~line 160)
Finding: The inline fallback now accepts `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`/`PLUGIN_ROOT` and computes `Path(plugin_root)/".."/".."/"shared"`. Under the Codex umbrella bundle the plugin root IS the bundle root, where `shared/` lives at `<root>/shared`, not `<root>/../../shared`. So under Codex this hook still resolves no shared root and silently no-ops — exactly the "permanently dark in production" defect AC3 claims this iterate fixes, recurring on the Codex side. The spec's Out of Scope names phase-recognition only; this gap is not disclosed anywhere. (It may also fail under a real Claude cache install, where `../../shared` from the version dir points at the marketplace dir — the new test only proves it against a monorepo-shaped fixture.)
Suggestion: Either add a `<root>/shared` candidate to the loop (cheap, matches the bundle layout the builder emits), or explicitly disclose this hook as dark under the Codex bundle in the spec/docs, the way phase recognition is.

**2. Category: spec — Severity: low**
File: `shared/scripts/tools/build_codex_plugin.py` (`BUILD_MANIFEST.json` write, ~line 230)
Finding: The spec's Affected Boundaries and mini-plan both promise a build manifest that is a "source→bundled-file map"; the emitted manifest is only `bundled-relative-path -> sha256` with no source provenance. The verifier compensates by rebuilding fresh, so AC5 still holds functionally, but the declared producer/consumer contract (verifier consumes a source→bundled map) is not what shipped.
Suggestion: Either add the source path per entry to the manifest or correct the spec/boundary description to match the hash-tree + fresh-rebuild design.

**3. Category: bug — Severity: low**
File: `shared/scripts/tools/verify_codex_plugin_bundle.py` (`main`, ~line 80)
Finding: `main()` catches only `BundleCollisionError`, while `build_bundle` (invoked inside `verify_bundle`) can also raise `UnsafeOutputPathError` (e.g. if the live `--bundle-dir` parent contains a foreign marketplace.json, the fresh build writes one into the temp parent — that path is safe, but a collision raised in `build_hook_inventory` from the *source tree* surfaces as `UnsafeOutputPathError` paths too). The builder's own `main()` was fixed to catch both (documented in the spec, item 11); the verifier was not given the same treatment, so a refusal surfaces as a raw traceback instead of `error: ...`.
Suggestion: Add `UnsafeOutputPathError` to the verifier's `except` clause.

**4. Category: test — Severity: low**
File: `shared/tests/test_capture_session_id.py` (`test_outputs_plugin_root_from_codex_native_var`), `shared/tests/test_audit_compliance_on_stop.py`, `shared/tests/test_audit_phase_quality_stop_hook_direct.py` (the new "codex native" tests)
Finding: The new Codex-native tests delenv `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` but do not delenv `SHIPWRIGHT_PLUGIN_ROOT`. Since the resolver checks `SHIPWRIGHT_PLUGIN_ROOT` first, an ambient value in the test environment would be resolved instead of the intended `PLUGIN_ROOT`, and the assertions on the injected/recognized value would fail (or, for the compliance test, silently exercise the wrong branch). `test_plugin_root.py` gets this right with an autouse `_clean_env` fixture; these three do not.
Suggestion: Add `monkeypatch.delenv("SHIPWRIGHT_PLUGIN_ROOT", raising=False)` to each of the three new tests (or replicate the autouse fixture).

**5. Category: spec — Severity: low**
File: `.shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-09-20-codex-plugin-bundle-root-contract-miniplan.md` (§1, §2 step 2)
Finding: The mini-plan remains internally stale: §1/step 2 say only `capture_session_id.py` "needed migrating" and treat the two audit hooks as unchanged, while AC3/the final code migrate all three to the shared resolver. This exact inconsistency was flagged by both external reviewers (glm medium, openai high) and the spec's triage section records it as addressed in the spec text — but the mini-plan file committed in this diff still carries the stale wording.
Suggestion: Add a one-line "superseded — see AC3" note to mini-plan §1/step 2, per the reviewers' own suggestion.

Already-disclosed items (raw-filesystem copy, symlink/determinism hardening, unvalidated `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` hook execution under Codex, `_merge_preserving_order` spurious-refusal shape) are recorded in the spec with dispositions; I do not re-raise them as new defects.

## Overall assessment

The core deliverables are sound and unusually well-evidenced; the one finding worth fixing before ship is the cleanup hook's `../../shared` traversal, which quietly reintroduces the exact "permanently dark hook" defect this iterate set out to fix, now on the Codex side — ship-with-fixes (finding 1 plus the small test-hygiene fix in finding 4).

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

openai.feedback:
- Category: security  
  Severity: medium  
  File: [build_codex_plugin.py](C:/Users/SvenRoth/AppData/Local/Temp/shipwright-codex-review-a75ri851/shared/scripts/tools/build_codex_plugin.py:109)  
  Finding: `_copy_tree()` follows symlinks by default and neither it nor `_hash_tree()` rejects or records symlinks. A symlink inside `shared/`, a skill, or plugin scripts can therefore package content outside the declared source tree; a symlinked directory in the built bundle may also evade the hash-based verifier entirely. This violates AC5’s path-escape/traceability guarantee.  
  Suggestion: Reject symlinks in all copied trees, or resolve each target and require it to remain within its declared source root; make the verifier explicitly flag symlinks.

- Category: bug  
  Severity: medium  
  File: [cleanup-review-scratch-on-code-reviewer-failure.py](C:/Users/SvenRoth/AppData/Local/Temp/shipwright-codex-review-a75ri851/plugins/shipwright-build/scripts/hooks/cleanup-review-scratch-on-code-reviewer-failure.py:169)  
  Finding: The cleanup hook still derives shared code only as `<plugin-root>/../../shared`. In the bundled Codex layout, `PLUGIN_ROOT`/`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is the umbrella bundle root and shared code is at `<plugin-root>/shared`; the current calculation points outside the bundle and the hook silently no-ops.  
  Suggestion: Resolve `<plugin-root>/shared` first for the umbrella bundle, then retain the legacy `../../shared` fallback for Claude-cache installs. Add a Codex-bundle-layout test.

- Category: regression  
  Severity: medium  
  File: [codex_hook_inventory.py](C:/Users/SvenRoth/AppData/Local/Temp/shipwright-codex-review-a75ri851/shared/scripts/tools/codex_hook_inventory.py:132)  
  Finding: Command hooks are merged solely by their plugin-relative invoked-script path and invocation tokens; the implementation never compares the contents of same-path scripts from different plugin origins. If two plugins contain different `scripts/hooks/foo.py` implementations but register the same command, the bundle emits only the first origin’s command and silently drops the other behavior, whereas Claude would run both.  
  Suggestion: Hash equivalent same-relative-path source scripts before merging and raise `BundleCollisionError` when they differ, unless the command is intentionally namespaced per origin. Add a fixture with divergent script contents.

- Category: spec  
  Severity: medium  
  File: [build_codex_plugin.py](C:/Users/SvenRoth/AppData/Local/Temp/shipwright-codex-review-a75ri851/shared/scripts/tools/build_codex_plugin.py:207)  
  Finding: `BUILD_MANIFEST.json` contains only bundled-path-to-hash entries, not the specified source-to-bundled-file map. The verifier compensates by rebuilding, but the declared producer/consumer format and required traceability artifact are not implemented.  
  Suggestion: Record each bundled file’s declared source path(s), destination path, and hash in the manifest, and test that mapping for skills, origin scripts, and shared files.

Ship with fixes: core bundle construction is substantial, but source-tree escape handling and the Codex-layout cleanup regression need correction before approval.
